channel.title: N722BD Accident Monitor (EN)
channel.description: Running overview of public information on the Learjet 60 N722BD accident in Palm Beach County, Florida (1 Nov 2026). Distinguishes official, data, media and unconfirmed reports.

item.title: [Unconfirmed] CBS12: about 600 residents remain displaced; NTSB to hold briefing
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (page not read directly), around 600 Greenacres residents remain displaced or assisted by authorities after the crash, and the NTSB is due to hold a briefing in West Palm Beach on Monday. Results also mention a Bombardier statement supporting the investigation; the cause and any role of weather are not yet determined. (Source: CBS12 (WPEC))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Operator and flight rules (Part 91 / 135) unclear
item.description: [Unconfirmed] IBTimes UK reports that N722BD appears in charter listings under Aurora Aviation's Part 135 certificate, but officials have not confirmed whether the flight was a charter; Austin airport described the aircraft as private. Unconfirmed, single source. Discrepancy: serial number 60-271 (registry / IBTimes) vs 60-186 (charter site FlyUSA, per search results). (Source: International Business Times UK)

item.title: [Data] Registered owner of N722BD: LR60271 LLC (Wilmington, DE)
item.description: [Data] FlightAware (read directly) lists LR60271 LLC of Wilmington, Delaware, as owner of N722BD; flight history is hidden at the owner/operator's request. The registered owner does not show who operated the flight. (Source: FlightAware)

item.title: [Media] FlightGlobal: “high-energy” accident, photo of responders at scene
item.description:
[Media] FlightGlobal (only the intro read directly, rest behind paywall) calls it a high-energy accident after a high-speed dive; US investigators are starting a probe. The article carries a photo of emergency services at the scene. (Source: FlightGlobal)
Photo: Emergency services at the accident site (Palm Beach County Fire Rescue, via FlightGlobal)

item.title: [Media] ABC: impact near Military Trail in Greenacres, descent about 350 ft/s
item.description:
[Media] Citing the FAA, ABC News reports a rapid descent of about 350 feet per second; the aircraft was 22 years old. According to local authorities it came down near Military Trail between Cresthaven Blvd and 10th Avenue in the Greenacres area, leaving a crater near a shopping centre. (Source: ABC News)
Photo: Flames at the crash site, Palm Beach County, 1 Nov 2026 (Eduin Cruz / Reuters, via ABC News)

item.title: [Media] NBC: all 9 on board killed; ATC audio with mayday call
item.description: [Media] According to NBC News, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said all 9 people on board died; the victims have not been identified. NBC describes ATC audio in which the crew reports light ice and moderate turbulence, then a mayday and descent of 10,000 and later 20,000 ft/min. Governor DeSantis said, per NBC, there were no reports of injuries on the ground. (Source: NBC News)

item.title: [Unconfirmed] NTSB launching go-team, briefing Monday in West Palm Beach
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (the X post was not read directly), the NTSB announced a go-team; investigators were due on Sunday and Monday morning, with a media briefing on Monday in West Palm Beach. Location wording differs between sources: NTSB “Lake Worth Beach”, FAA “Cresthaven”, sheriff Military Trail between Cresthaven Blvd and 10th Ave N. (Source: NTSB Newsroom (X))

item.title: [Data] FR24: steep right-hand descent, last return 8,750 ft at 17:49:22Z
item.description: [Data] According to FR24 ADS-B data (read directly), N722BD (Learjet 60, built 2004) departed Austin at 15:37Z; at 17:48Z it briefly climbed, then entered a steep right-hand descent. The last altitude received was 8,750 ft at 17:49:22Z, with vertical rate above 32,000 ft/min. In ATC audio reviewed by FR24, the crew had earlier reported icing, moderate turbulence and precipitation and requested a climb to FL370. (Source: Flightradar24 Blog)

item.title: [Official] FAA: Learjet 60 crashed near Cresthaven, 9 people on board
item.description: [Official] According to the FAA statement (read directly), a Learjet 60 crashed into a residential area near Cresthaven, Florida, at about 12:50 local time on 1 Nov. It was flying from Austin-Bergstrom (Texas) to North Eleuthera (Bahamas) with 9 people on board. The NTSB leads the investigation with FAA involvement. (Source: FAA – Newsroom)
